_doc:
Canonical ML foundational papers that should always surface as ancestor edges when they appear in a seed's referenced_works. Bypasses LLM classification — if a seed's parent matches one of these patterns, emit a stable 'extends' edge so the research lineage is structurally visible. See paperpilot/scripts/_lineage_classify.py::_is_foundational_ancestor + issue #277.

Why needed: OpenAlex-sourced references carry no S2 intent labels, so derive_relation's heuristic falls through to year/cite contrast, which only fires within a narrow delta range. Out of 53 references on the canonical ViT paper, only 6 surfaced (AIAYN via LLM, a few via year/cite). AlexNet, ResNet, BiT, DETR, iGPT — all clearly within the research lineage — got dropped because the LLM (with no intent hint) tended to classify them as unrelated. This file makes that explicit: 'these papers are canonical ancestors; preserve the edge regardless of what the heuristic or LLM thinks'.

Scope: kept tight (~25 entries) so we don't fabricate edges for everything. Only papers that are universally recognised as research-lineage anchors in ML/CV/NLP make the list. New entries require a justification in the PR description.
